name: The Human Edge: Tech & Human Flourishing
partiful_description:
Technology is changing how we work, connect, create, and live—often at a pace that our bodies and minds weren’t designed to match.

As we build the future, how do we make sure we’re also building lives that allow us to flourish within it?

Tech & Human Flourishing is an immersive wellness experience exploring the physical and mental practices that help us stay grounded, resilient, and fully human in an increasingly digital world.

We’ll begin with a 45-minute, all-levels strength training session using barbells, dumbbells, kettlebells, and light cardio. Through movement, we’ll explore strength not just as physical capacity but as a foundation for confidence, resilience, and long-term well-being.

Then we’ll shift from activation to recovery with a 30-minute nervous system reset, incorporating guided breathwork, mindfulness, and cognitive reframing practices to help you slow down, regulate stress, and create space for mental recovery.

We’ll close with time to connect and exchange ideas with others interested in the intersection of technology, health, and human flourishing.

What to expect:
👋 6:30–6:45 PM | Gather & Welcome (15 min)
Arrive, settle in, meet fellow participants, and set an intention for the evening.

🏋🏻‍♀️ 6:45–7:30 PM | Strength Training Session (45 min)
We'll move together through a guided strength training session featuring barbells, dumbbells, kettlebells, and light cardio. Designed for all levels, the session explores physical strength as a foundation for resilience, confidence, energy, and long-term well-being.

Whether you're new to strength training or an experienced athlete, we'll focus on moving with intention and building capacity—not simply pushing harder.

😮‍💨 7:30–8:00 PM | Nervous System Reset (30 min)
We'll transition from activation to recovery through guided breathwork, mindfulness, and cognitive reframing practices designed to support nervous system regulation, reduce stress, and create space for mental clarity and recovery.

🤝 8:00–8:30 PM | Closing & Networking (30 min)
Come together to reflect, connect, and exchange ideas with fellow participants exploring the intersection of technology, health, and human flourishing.

No prior strength training or mindfulness experience is required.

Come move. Come reset. Come explore what it means to flourish in the future we're building.

name: Digital Asset Strategy Roundtable
partiful_description:
As the U.S. digital asset regulatory landscape evolves, firms should translate policy signals into strategy across product, capital, and operating model design. California’s Digital Financial Assets Law (DFAL), which will require many firms serving California residents to be licensed or to have submitted a complete application as of July 1, 2026, offers a near-term signal of how regulators may approach licensing, custody, governance, and consumer protection within an emerging supervisory framework. At the same time, the GENIUS Act has established a federal framework for payment stablecoins, reinforcing their growing importance across both digital and traditional ecosystems. Lessons from NYDFS's 2022 Stablecoin Guidance were instrumental in shaping the legislative conversations around GENIUS. How will DFAL's implementation shape the CLARITY conversations?

​In October, BRG and the California Blockchain Advocacy Coalition will host a private, invitation-only roundtable in San Francisco for senior leaders from financial institutions, fintechs, and digital asset firms to discuss how these developments should shape mid- and long-term business strategy. The conversation will focus on product roadmap, capital and liquidity planning, operating model choices, and partnership strategy as firms pursue federal charter pathways while continuing to navigate state-level regimes such as DFAL. The session will be co-hosted by Michael Hollerich, Managing Director at BRG, and Joe Ciccolo, Executive Director of the California Blockchain Advocacy Coalition, bringing complementary industry, regulatory, and policy perspectives to the discussion. The roundtable is designed to foster peer-level dialogue among a small group of senior executives and will be conducted under Chatham House-style rules to encourage open and candid exchange.

name: Hype v. Hesitancy: Exploring Silicon Valley’s AI Confidence Gap
partiful_description:
As part of SF Tech Week, Weber Shandwick will host a timely, stirring panel discussion led by Megan Morrone, Technology Editor at CNBC exploring the growing cultural chasm between Silicon Valley’s embrace of AI and the general public sentiment.

This delta is reflective of a broader debate that pits seemingly enthusiastic advocates against cautious critics of AI. While the Bay Tech sector accelerates into an AI-first reality, mainstream sentiment outside the tech epicenter remains cautious. The broader public continues to actively wrestle with AI’s nuanced challenges like ethical boundaries, algorithmic bias, IP rights, and workforce impact.

This session will bring together industry voices whose work addresses these urgent realities to dissect the geographic and cultural disconnect and examine how the tech industry can bridge the gap between relentless AI optimism and societal hesitancy. Our panelists will each bring a unique perspective to the conversation, aiming to address why these challenges exist and how to navigate them, using examples from their everyday work in technology.

name: Will AI Really Replace Your Doctor?
partiful_description:
AI can already interpret scans, summarize medical records, suggest diagnoses, answer health questions, and in some cases outperform clinicians on specific tasks. So where does that leave the human doctor?

Join us for a provocative conversation about what happens when AI moves from being a tool for doctors to something that starts looking a lot like the doctor itself.

We’ll explore questions like: Would you trust an AI with a diagnosis? What happens when AI knows your health history better than any physician ever could? Which parts of medicine can actually be automated—and which fundamentally require a human? Who is responsible when an AI gets it wrong? And will the future be AI vs. doctors, or doctors + AI?

name: Open to Work: The Game Show
partiful_description:
A live game show and networking night built around the one thing everyone in the room has in common: the job hunt.

Here's the bit. You apply to a fake job with your real resume. The room votes on who advances. Survivors get sixty seconds on stage to pitch themselves. Finalists sit for a live panel interview where the panel holds your actual resume and a set of loaded questions — plus a workplace scandal you know nothing about. Half the room can see what the other half can't. That gap is where the comedy lives.

Underneath the bit, it's networking that actually works. The crowd hears real career summaries during voting, strangers sell themselves to a room of peers, and nobody has to cold-approach anyone. The show manufactures the introductions. Speed networking, minus the speed dating energy.

Everything runs in your phone's browser, live and in sync with the host. No downloads, no accounts. Scan and you're in.

The fine print, in marker: the humor is workplace satire — layoffs, interview loops, corporate absurdity. Every scandal is fictional and generated fresh per show. Nobody's real resume goes on screen without their approval, from their own phone.

One winner, hired on the spot, for a job that does not exist. Compensation: bragging rights, fully vested. Then the real networking hour starts.

name: The Longevity Blind Spot: Why Mental + Metabolic Health May Define Your Healthspan
partiful_description:
The longevity conversation has exploded - biomarkers, wearables, sleep, nutrition, GLP-1s, supplements, biological age and increasingly sophisticated ways to measure and optimize our bodies.

But are we overlooking one of the biggest pieces of healthspan: the connection between our mental and metabolic health?

For decades, healthcare has largely treated mental health and physical health as separate problems. Yet a growing body of research is uncovering important links between mental health, metabolism, inflammation, insulin resistance, hormones, sleep, energy regulation and the way our brains function.

So what happens when we start looking at them together?

Join us for a provocative conversation about mental health, metabolic health, longevity and the future of healthcare.

We’ll explore questions like: Could metabolic health help explain why some people struggle with mental health despite treatment? How much can labs, wearables and longitudinal health data actually tell us? Where is the science strong, and where is the hype getting ahead of the evidence? What role will AI play in connecting the dots across our health? And if we improve mental and metabolic health earlier in life, could we meaningfully increase not just how long we live, but how many of those years we live well?

Maybe the next frontier of longevity isn’t just living longer. It’s understanding the connection between the brain and the rest of the body.

You've been tokenmaxxing since Monday. Time to cash out: DJ, drinks, and the people you meant to meet all week, finally in one room.

Brief remarks from C1 and friends up top (brief - we promise), then it's a party until 9. No panels, no demos, no thought leadership. We did that Monday-Thursday. This is the close-out the week deserves.

THE NIGHT
5:00 — doors
6:00 — remarks, ten minutes max
6:10 — party

Last RSVP of the week. Make it count. rsvpmaxx accordingly.

Hosted by Efficient Frontier Labs at C1

name: Making the Agentic Web OPEN for business
formats: Breakfast, Brunch or Lunch; Networking; Panel / Fireside Chat
partiful_description:

name: Sunday Signals: AI, Risk & Real Estate
partiful_description:
Join VeriCasa and LSEG for an intimate Sunday brunch during San Francisco Tech Week, bringing together leaders across AI, RegTech, PropTech, financial services and real estate.

As AI moves deeper into regulated industries, the conversation is shifting from experimentation to infrastructure: how do we make automated decisions faster without losing trust, transparency or accountability?

Over brunch, we’ll explore how AI-native platforms, trusted data and risk intelligence are reshaping KYC, AML, compliance and real estate transactions and what the next generation of regulated workflows will look like.

No long presentations. No conference theatre.

Just good food, sharp people and a practical conversation about where AI, risk and real estate are going next.

Hosted by VeriCasa × LSEG Sunday · San Francisco Tech WeekLimited attendance · RSVP required

This event is a part of #SFTechWeek, a week of events hosted by the top founders, funds, and companies to bring together the tech ecosystem. Learn more at www.tech-week.com.

name: Ulysses: The Ocean Company
primary_host: SF Blue Tech, Ulysses: The Ocean Company
partiful_description:
The ocean economy is witnessing structural transformation, with maritime submersibles and autonomous vessels rapidly moving from niche to strategic and defense roles. As global reliance on ocean infrastructure deepens, unmanned vessels and underwater robotics are stepping to the fore.

This vertical is HOT. San Francisco counts several firms that operate and manufacture locally.

View products and hear from Ulysses' COO Colm O'Brien. Customers include U.S. Navy, government of Australia, Great Barrier Reef Foundation and The Nature Conservancy.

Backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Booz Allen Ventures, Harpoon Ventures, peeblebed, Lowercarbon Capital, Genius Ventures, Onto Ventures, Superorganism and others: $48 million raised

** defense, surveillance, national security, ocean exploration, maritime navigation, coastal regeneration, ports and shipping, fisheries, aquaculture, submersibles, robotics, unmanned vessels, autonomous vessels, uncrewed vessels, data science, ports and marinas **

Hosted by SF Blue Tech, a member-based group with focus on blue economy, marine and ocean technology, www.sfbluetech.com
